introduction.problem_before: Rendering a chooser in a narrow area could wrap navigation labels across lines. The component comment describes wrapped content keeping the panel narrow on later frames.
introduction.change: Set TextWrapMode::Extend in nav_button so every shared subscreen chooser requests unwrapped labels.
introduction.example_before_after: A label such as "Token Creator" could previously occupy multiple lines; it now requests a single line even when the available width is narrow.

steps.title: Disable wrapping in navigation buttons
steps.called_by: When Tokens, Tools or DashPay renders its chooser, add_subscreen_chooser_panel calls nav_button for each navigation item.
steps.decides: The button explicitly uses TextWrapMode::Extend rather than leaving its wrapping mode unspecified.
steps.next: The shared panel adds the returned button to its UI, reads clicked(), and returns the selected item's AppAction.
steps.why: Applying the policy in the shared builder gives all chooser labels the same wrapping behavior.

annotations.was: Constructed the button without an explicit wrap-mode override.
annotations.is: Explicitly sets the button's wrap mode to TextWrapMode::Extend.

annotations.text: The token regression test asserts single-line button height and consistent panel width across token screens after narrow-to-wide resizing. These assertions were read, not executed.

impact_refs.reason: Every navigation item is rendered through nav_button before its click dispatches the associated action.
The non-resizable Tokens chooser receives the shared button wrapping policy.
The vertically scrollable Tools chooser receives the shared button wrapping policy.
The resizable DashPay chooser also receives the shared button wrapping policy.
